title: Measured exposure and observed outcomes
kind: Complete selected excerpts from the current saved chat response
markdown:
### Exposure measurement

- LactMed reports generally low sertraline concentrations in breast milk. The metabolite **norsertraline** was often detectable at low levels in infant serum. [S10](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK501191/)

### Observed infant outcomes

- Several small observational groups reported no observed acute adverse effects, and one group reported normal infant weight gain through 6 months. The retrieved LactMed metadata does not establish a study count; missing study counts are unknown, not zero. [S10](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK501191/)

### Selected product label

The selected DailyMed product is **SERTRALINE HYDROCHLORIDE TABLET [REMEDYREPACK INC.]**, with an effective date of November 5, 2026. The exact product and formulation match was not confirmed. [S1](https://dailymed.nlm.nih.gov/dailymed/lookup.cfm?setid=687ebdc4-6946-454e-8d46-3207488ccf32)
narration: This is a replay of the current saved response. It separates measured milk and infant exposure from observed infant outcomes, with direct source links. The full answer also identifies missing and truncated sections, the selected manufacturer label, and uncertainty about study counts. LactMed covers lactation only.

title: A crisis cue stops the medication workflow
kind: Current fixed response; no model answer, research or participation
question: I feel hopeless since giving birth and think my baby would be better off without me. Can I take sertraline?
markdown:
You deserve support. I cannot answer this as a medication research question. Please call or text 988 (Suicide & Crisis Lifeline) for support now. If you or someone else is in immediate danger, call 911. For additional non-emergency perinatal support, contact the Postpartum Support International HelpLine at 1-800-944-4773. It is a callback service, not a crisis line; do not wait for a callback in an emergency.
Source: https://988lifeline.org?oai_link_source=model_response_hotline
Source: https://postpartum.net/get-help/

title: Empty retrieval carries an explicit boundary

json.message: No evidence retrieved; not evidence of safety.

narration: The synthetic no-match lookup returns machine-readable absence fields. No evidence retrieved is not evidence of safety. The model should preserve that distinction rather than turning a missing result into reassurance.

title: Questions prepare the clinician conversation
kind: Preparation questions from the current evidence brief
markdown:
- Does this evidence apply to my exact medicine, formulation, and all active ingredients?
- How closely do the study populations match the pregnancy context, including age and prematurity where relevant?
- Which findings measure exposure, and which measure clinical outcomes?
- What uncertainties or missing evidence should we discuss before making a treatment decision?
- What questions about benefits, risks, and follow-up should we address together?
narration: The brief returns questions to ask a clinician about the exact product, the relevant population, exposure versus outcomes, missing evidence and follow-up. These questions are authored by the prototype. They are preparation, not a medication plan.

title: Clinical review must assess the impression an answer creates
kind: S2 and S6 remain partially addressed
markdown:
### S2: No reports can read as safe

Study types and unknown study counts travel with the evidence. They do not establish adequate study quality or sample size.

### S6: Adverse facts can prompt stopping

Source context and a standing medication-change caution reduce one-sided framing. Two new evaluation cases examine this risk.

### Remaining requirement

A clinician must review real answers for false reassurance and alarm. No clinical review has occurred.
narration: Two safety risks need special emphasis. No reported effects can sound safe even when evidence is thin. Adverse findings can also prompt someone to stop a needed medicine. The payload preserves source context and includes a medication-change caution, and two new cases test framing. These are partial controls. A clinician must review real answers for reassurance and alarm that code checks cannot judge.
